title: Cognitive load reduction: review vignettes & quick tactics
content:
Quick note: purpose = capture small, repeatable heuristics and very short example vignettes that I can paste into PR comments or share with new reviewers. Not a full playbook, more a pocket reference / brain dump.

Top-level ideas (TL;DR):
- Reduce cognitive load by surfacing intent first: a one-line summary of the change + one-sentence rationale at top of PR comment.
- Break large PRs into oriented vignettes: what I expect to be safe to review in <10 min, and what needs deeper system-level verification.
- Use tiny, deterministic checks to gate complexity (e.g. snapshot of observable surface area: routes added, public API changes, DB migrations).

Vignettes (short examples to copy-paste):
1) "Behavior-first" opening for reviewers:
   - Summary: rename request router -> unified router to unify k/v cache paths; no semantic change to endpoints.
   - Why: reduces duplication for cache lookup logic and paves way for multi-model routing.
   - Quick smoke: run ./scripts/integration-smoke.sh --router-unified and ./scripts/sanity-checks.sh, expect 0 failures.
   - Areas to focus: concurrency around KV cache eviction (line ~240), new tests added under test/router/verify-unified.

2) "Small refactor split" guidance for authors:
   - If a refactor changes >1 package boundary (eg serving-runtime + observability) split into: (A) pure refactor commit with no behavior change + tests; (B) behavior change commit. Reviewers: accept A fast, focus attention on B.

Heuristics checklist (bite-sized, use in PR checklist):
- [ ] Does PR title explain intent (not implementation)? (e.g., "reduce memory footprint for long-ctx KV cache")
- [ ] One-line consumer-visible change? If none, say so explicitly.
- [ ] List of modified public interfaces (functions/classes/endpoints).
- [ ] Any DB or schema migrations? If yes, include rollback steps and migration window.
- [ ] New async paths: add timeout and retry behavior notes.
- [ ] Add small acceptance test that replicates critical behavior (deterministic).

Signal-to-noise reduction tactics (practical):
- Use the PR description template: Summary / Smoke / Risks / Backstop tests. If author leaves section blank, nudge them to fill before review.
- Encourage authors to mark "review surface" with code links: direct links to files + line ranges. This beats asking reviewers to hunt around.
- If a change touches many files but the diff is mostly mechanical (rename/export) ask for a short diff-filtered view showing only non-mechanical hunks.

Rollback triggers (when to escalate fast):
- Any change that affects token routing or model selection policy (high blast radius).
- Any migration requiring cluster-wide coordinated rollout.
- Observable latency regression >10% in perf CI for the last 3 runs.

One-line templates (quick snippets to paste):
- For authors asking for a quick review: "Quick pass requested: focus on lines X-Y for possible edge-case N; everything else is mechanical. Smoke script: ./smoke.sh --subset=routing"
- For reviewers requesting tests: "Can you add a deterministic unit that covers case <X> and a small e2e smoke that exercises <Y>? Without these I'd prefer a small canary rollout."

Open questions / things to experiment with (notes to self):
- Should we adopt a lightweight checklist bot that refuses merges unless Summary+Smoke fields are filled? Pros/cons: reduces noise but could block fast patch fixes.
- Try a weekly "review sprint" channel for larger refactors: short async sessions where authors post guided review links and reviewers sign up.
- Auto-generate a one-line behavioral diff (public API changes) from git diff metadata. Is that feasible with our current tooling?

Follow-ups / Action items (me):
- Draft a PR description template with explicit "smoke steps" and "backout plan" fields. (TODO by 2026-03-07)
- Prototype a tiny CLI that opens a GitHub PR with prefilled Summary/Smoke fields from commit message. (spike)
- Try the "vignette" format on my next large refactor, measure reviewer time-to-first-comment.

Notes to self: keep these items terse. When in doubt, prefer a short example that a teammate can copy/paste into a PR or comment.

Random scratch ideas to explore later:
- A mini-DSL for "review focus" annotations in code comments that tools can surface in PRs.
- Train new reviewers with 5-minute puzzles: give them a noisy diff and ask them to produce a 3-line review summary. Track improvement.

End of dump.

Unresolved: whether this belongs under eng-developer-experience drive or lives in shared drive templates. For now keep in users as a personal scratchpad until I test the format.
